request: Irrigate: a Settler irrigates the Plain it stands on when it has Water among its four neighbours and is not irrigated; it spends the Settler's remaining moves and the tile yields one more food; the HUD lists the action with the irrigation icon and the tile card shows the icon and 'Irrigated' on its units line

laneOnBase.B: fails only the stage's icon and units-line checks (3)
laneOnBase.C: fails the same 3 and the press check (the store's typed switch of actions answered 'The HUD does not know the action irrigate')

B.laneAfter: CIVLITE_UI_NATIVE_PASSED: 161 + 28 probe checks on the native HUD; 49 + 23 oracle mutations (rerun by the orchestrator on the branch)

C.laneAfter: CIVLITE_UI_LANE_PASSED: 161 + 28 + 41 probe checks; 49 + 23 + 38 oracle mutations and 23 of the scan (rerun by the orchestrator on the branch)

rule: decisionRule.singleObservation of the protocol: one implementation per arm, so no interval; each measure's category from the difference C - B against 10% of B's value (gain below -margin, cost above +margin, neutral within); the axis takes a category only when the four agree
confounds: the order is fixed (B first, C second), not drawn, and with one observation per arm it is not balanced

the time includes the HUD lane's run, and the lane file runs both arms: on each arm's branch the other arm is the one still red, and it fails at a different point, so the lane took about 114 s on B's branch and 276 s on C's; without the lane the two arms took about 1.0 and 1.1 minutes
the base already holds the game rule, the icon and the lane's expectation, so each arm's work is the HUD's part only; the request is small, and a single small request says little about larger ones

the two HUDs differ structurally on one point the request touched: the native HUD dispatches an action by its method name, while the React Native store dispatches through a typed switch, so C had to add a case to ui/store.ts and B had nothing to add there
statement: one observation per arm: it supports a description, not a statistical claim
